subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is a key part of natural selection?
options: Organisms choosing to change to suit their environment
All organisms in a species being identical
Characteristics changing only within one lifetime
Individuals with advantageous variations are more likely to survive and reproduce
questions.explain: In natural selection, individuals with advantageous inherited variations survive, reproduce and pass on those alleles.

questions.q: Whose work is most associated with the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explain: Charles Darwin proposed evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species'.

questions.q: The rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is evidence for evolution because:
options: Resistant bacteria survive antibiotics and reproduce, so resistance spreads
Antibiotics create resistant bacteria from nothing
questions.explain: Resistant bacteria survive and reproduce by natural selection, demonstrating evolution happening quickly.

questions.q: Which is a real example of genetic engineering?
options: Dogs bred for a calm temperament
Bacteria modified to produce human insulin
questions.explain: Bacteria can be genetically modified to make human insulin, used to treat diabetes.

questions.q: Which of these could cause a species to become extinct?
options: A new predator or disease and loss of habitat
questions.explain: New predators, disease, habitat destruction or environmental change can all drive a species to extinction.

questions.q: The three-domain system, proposed by Carl Woese, divides life into:
questions.explain: Woese used genetic analysis to propose three domains: Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota.

questions.q: Why did it take a long time for Darwin's theory to be widely accepted?
options: It conflicted with religious beliefs and the mechanism of inheritance was not yet known
No one was interested in biology
questions.explain: Darwin's theory challenged religious views and lacked a known mechanism of inheritance (genes were not yet understood).

options: Breeding two organisms over many generations
Exposing organisms to sunlight to change genes
Transferring a gene from one organism into another
questions.explain: Genetic engineering transfers genes from one organism into another, e.g. inserting a human gene into bacteria.

questions.q: In the binomial naming system, an organism is named using its:
questions.explain: Binomial names use the genus (first, capitalised) and species (second), e.g. Homo sapiens.

questions.q: One disadvantage of selective breeding is that it:
options: Can reduce genetic variation, increasing the risk of disease
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces variation (inbreeding), making organisms more vulnerable to disease.

questions.q: Carl Linnaeus classified living things into groups starting with the largest, the kingdom. Which order is correct (largest to smallest)?
options: Species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom
Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
questions.explain: The Linnaean order from largest to smallest is kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

questions.q: A potential concern about GM crops is that:
options: They cannot be eaten at all
They can never increase crop yields
They make crops grow more slowly always
Transplanted genes might spread to wild plants, and long-term effects are uncertain
questions.explain: Concerns about GM crops include genes spreading to wild populations and uncertain long-term health/ecological effects.
